proposals.before: In the first year of Jiaqing he was ordered to take three thousand garrison troops and join Banner Commander Yongbao in campaigning against the White Lotus rebels in Hubei.
proposals.after: In the first year of Jiaqing he was ordered to take three thousand garrison troops and join Banner Commander Yongbao in campaigning against the sectarian rebels in Hubei.
proposals.reason: Chinese 教匪 means sectarian/religious rebels; 'White Lotus' is an interpretive gloss not in the source wording.

proposals.before: The rebels slipped into Pengzhou and secretly allied with Ran Wenbi to raid Yilong; Heng Rui held Mopanzhai and, with Huiling and others, struck them down; Wenbi fled, Long Shaozhou of Shaanxi joined him, and together they were beaten at Yangjiazhai.
proposals.after: The rebels slipped into Pengzhou and secretly allied with Ran Wenchou to raid Yilong; Heng Rui held Mopanzhai and, with Huiling and others, struck them down; Wenchou fled, Long Shaozhou of Shaanxi joined him, and together they were beaten at Yangjiazhai.
proposals.reason: Chinese 冉文儔 / 文儔 is Wenchou, not Wenbi; English mistransliterates the personal name.

proposals.before: Qing Cheng, of the Sun clan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain White Banner, great-great-grandson of Provincial Commander Sike and grandson of Banner Commander Wufu.
proposals.after: Qing Cheng, of the Sun clan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain White Banner, great-grandson of Provincial Commander Sike and grandson of Banner Commander Wufu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 曾孫 means great-grandson (third generation down), not great-great-grandson.

proposals.before: Heng Rui had been campaigning since the White Lotus rebellion began, often leading detached columns against major enemy forces, but by now he was old and ill and had long gone without a notable victory.
proposals.after: Heng Rui had been campaigning since the sectarian rebellion began, often leading detached columns against major enemy forces, but by now he was old and ill and had long gone without a notable victory.
proposals.reason: Source 教匪 is sectarian rebels; White Lotus is an interpretive gloss not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: In Jiaqing's first year he led troops to Nanyang and Xiangyang against the White Lotus rebels and, with Heng Rui, repeatedly defeated Yao Zhifu and Liu Zhixie at Shuanggou and Zhangjiaji.
proposals.after: In Jiaqing's first year he led troops to Nanyang and Xiangyang against the sectarian rebels and, with Heng Rui, repeatedly defeated Yao Zhifu and Liu Zhixie at Shuanggou and Zhangjiaji.
proposals.reason: Chinese 教匪 means sectarian rebels; White Lotus is an added gloss.

proposals.before: When the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai raided Baoning and Luo Qiqing and Ran Wenbi pillaged eastern Sichuan, he was ordered into Sichuan to campaign jointly with Yimian.
proposals.after: When the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai raided Baoning and Luo Qiqing and Ran Wenchou pillaged eastern Sichuan, he was ordered into Sichuan to campaign jointly with Yimian.
proposals.reason: 冉文儔 is Wenchou, not Wenbi.

proposals.before: In Jiaqing's first year he went to Hubei against the White Lotus rebels; in the fourth month of the second year he chased them into Shaanxi and routed them at Zhoujiahe in Shanyang; he was made right vice commander of the Xi'an banner and given command of the Elite Vanguard Brigade.
proposals.after: In Jiaqing's first year he went to Hubei against the sectarian rebels; in the fourth month of the second year he chased them into Shaanxi and routed them at Zhoujiahe in Shanyang; he was made right vice commander of the Xi'an banner and given command of the Elite Vanguard Brigade.
proposals.reason: 教匪 is sectarian rebels; White Lotus is an interpretive gloss.

proposals.before: In Jiaqing's first year the White Lotus rebels Nie Jieren and Zhang Zhengmo rose at Zhijiang and Yidu; Governor Huiling held Taihe Mountain; Fu Zhina raced to join him, attacked Fenghuang Mountain, and captured Jieren.
proposals.after: In Jiaqing's first year the sectarian rebels Nie Jieren and Zhang Zhengmo rose at Zhijiang and Yidu; Governor Huiling held Taihe Mountain; Fu Zhina raced to join him, attacked Fenghuang Mountain, and captured Jieren.
proposals.reason: 教匪 means sectarian rebels; White Lotus is an added gloss.

proposals.before: In the third year White Lotus rebels probed Henan; Governor Wu Xiongguang held Lushi, but most of his troops had been sent elsewhere.
proposals.after: In the third year sectarian rebels probed Henan; Governor Wu Xiongguang held Lushi, but most of his troops had been sent elsewhere.
proposals.reason: 教匪 means sectarian rebels; White Lotus is an added gloss.

decisions.reason: In this Jiaqing campaign context 教匪 refers to the White Lotus rebels. The existing specific historical designation is accurate and more useful than the generic 'sectarian rebels.'
冉文儔 is Ran Wenchou; the existing Wenbi is a mistransliteration repeated within the sentence.
曾孫 means great-grandson, not great-great-grandson.
教匪 refers to the White Lotus rebels in this sustained Jiaqing campaign narrative; the established English wording is accurate.
The named leaders and Jiaqing setting identify these as White Lotus rebels; replacing the useful historical designation with a generic label would not improve the translation.
